title: Daisy and Otto's Berry Quest
markdown:
The sun peeked over the sleepy hills, painting the meadow with warm golden light. Daisy the lamb, soft wool and twitching ears, stretched her legs with a happy little baa. The grass tickled her nose, still damp with morning dew that sparkled like tiny jewels. A grand day for an adventure.

“What a lovely sunny morning.” Her voice like tiny bells. “I wonder what fun things it holds for me and my best friend, Otto.”

Just then Otto the otter came waddling along with a cheerful splash from the stream. Whiskers wiggling.

“Daisy, my dear Daisy. Did you hear the news? The little birds are chirping about it.”

A little bird, Pip, with feathers the colour of rainbow sherbet, landed on a nearby daisy.

“Tweet-tweet. Yes, yes.” Pip chirped. “The yummiest biggest berries grow on the other side of the Whispering Woods. So plump and purple, and they have dew that sparkles. But you must bring them back before the dew dries, or they’ll lose their sparkle and taste yucky.” He tilted his head, bright eyes gleaming.

Daisy’s eyes widened. Berries. And a race against the sun.

“Oh, Otto.” Her fluffy tail gave a little wiggle. “We must go. We must get those sparkly berries before the dew disappears.”

Otto puffed out his chest. “We really must. A basket of tasty berries, gathered with friendship, makes the best adventure. But is it too far? Will we be quick enough?”

Daisy thought, nose twitching. Then a determined little hop. “We’ll be quick if we work together. You’re fast in the water, and I’m good at scampering over the grass. A perfect berry-picking pair.”

“Hooray.” Otto did a little spin. “A perfect pair for a perfect quest.”

With a strong little basket tucked under Otto’s arm they set off. Daisy’s woolly hooves made soft thuds. Otto’s sleek body glided beside her. The sun climbed, painting the sky rosy pink and soft orange.

First a babbling brook, water giggling over smooth stones.

“Oh dear.” Daisy looked at the wide water. “How will we cross without getting wet?”

Otto grinned. “Easy peasy.” He nudged a sturdy fallen log that lay across like a bridge. “Hop on, Daisy. I’ll help you.”

She hopped onto the log. It wobbled a little, like a small boat, but Otto’s strong pushes from the bank kept it steady. Wibble-wobble. Daisy giggled, wool bouncing. They landed with a soft plop on the other side.

Next a field of giggly flowers, petals so soft they tickled Daisy’s nose and Otto’s whiskers.

“Achoo.” Otto sneezed a funny little puff, and Daisy laughed, little bells dancing. The flowers rustled their colourful heads in a gentle hello.

Deeper into the woods, where the trees stood tall, a cheerful chatter from high in an oak.

“Hello there, adventurers.” A busy squirrel held a shiny acorn on its nose. “Going for berries, are you? I know a quicker path. Follow the bend of the stream, then turn left at the big bumpy root that looks like a sleeping dragon.”

“Thank you, friend,” they called together. Much better than guessing.

Soon a clearing bathed in warm sunlight. Lots and lots of big purple berries, tiny dewdrops sparkling like jewels.

“Oh, they’re even more beautiful than Pip said.” Daisy’s eyes wide.

“Hooray.” Otto started carefully placing berries into the basket. Plink, plonk, plink. Sweet juicy scent filling the air.

Daisy noticed the sun was higher. The little dewdrops on the leaves were starting to disappear, shimmering away.

“Otto. The dew is going fast. We must be quick.”

He looked up. “Oh no. You’re right. We must hurry.”

They scurried back, the basket now heavy. Then they saw it. A wide shimmering puddle, much too big to jump, spread across the path like a shiny mirror.

“Oh my.” Daisy’s ears drooped a little. “How will we get the basket across? Too heavy to carry, and far too wide to jump.”

Otto peered into the water, nose twitching. “We can’t get around it quickly.” A little worried. Daisy pictured the beautiful berries losing their special sparkle.

Then she remembered. Ears perked. “The stream. And the big bumpy root that looked like a sleeping dragon. The squirrel’s shortcut.”

Otto’s eyes lit. “That’s it. The shortcut must lead us around this big puddle.”

“Quick, quick.” They scampered, following the winding path the squirrel had shown them. Sure enough, it led around the wide puddle and back onto the path toward home.

With a final burst they raced across the meadow. The sun shone brightly. The last few dewdrops were just beginning to fade. They reached their favourite sun-dappled spot, panting a little, right as the very last sparkle winked out.

“We did it.”

They sat down, the basket of plump purple berries between them, and shared the juicy fruit. Flavours bursting like sweet sunshine. Daisy sighed a contented little baa. Otto had a smear of purple juice on his whiskers. He did not say friendship was the sweetest thing of all. He only passed her another berry, and they ate until the basket was light again and the meadow was warm, which was thank-you enough for a dew that had waited just long enough.
